html:
The flight of about 700,000 Rohingya from Burma to Bangladesh from August 2017, after a campaign of killing, rape and burning by the Burmese army.

The Rohingya are a mostly Muslim people of Rakhine State, on the border with Bangladesh. Burma treats them as illegal migrants from Bengal, and a 1982 law left most of them without citizenship. They had faced waves of violence and expulsion before.

On 25 August 2017 a Rohingya armed group attacked police posts. The army answered with what it called clearance operations. Soldiers and local mobs killed thousands of people, raped women and girls, and burned hundreds of villages. Within weeks hundreds of thousands crossed into Bangladesh, where they crowded into camps near Cox's Bazar that grew into the largest refugee settlement in the world.

United Nations investigators said the army acted with genocidal intent. In 2019 The Gambia took Burma to the International Court of Justice, and Aung San Suu Kyi went to The Hague to defend her country. Most Rohingya refugees remain in the camps, unable to go home safely.
sum: The flight of about 700,000 Rohingya from Burma to Bangladesh from August 2017, after a campaign of killing, rape and burning by the Burmese army.
